source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC3 publishes one figure for its Prince William County campus: 2,232,875 square feet of technical space. No IT load in megawatts, no critical power figure, and no redundancy tier appear on the operator's spec page as retrieved. Without a published megawatt number, no honest translation into rack count or accelerator capacity is possible, and this site will not invent one.

The certifications field is empty in the published specifications. No Uptime Institute tier, no SOC attestation, and no ISO designation is listed on the page as read. What those absences mean for workload suitability is not determinable from the data alone.

Virginia has 326 mapped facilities, of which 19 publish a megawatt figure totaling 1,326 MW across those 19 sites. MCC3 is ranked twentieth by published megawatts, which in practice means it falls outside the ranked set entirely because it publishes no MW figure. The 2.2 million square feet of technical space is a large footprint by any ordinary measure, but until the operator publishes a power specification, this campus cannot be placed in the state's capacity picture with any precision.
